transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Jordan Li, Felix Moreno (Redwood); Dr. Anika Rao, Marco Diaz, Sana Patel, Terry Ng (Arborium)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll keep this tight 45 to 60, um goal is to validate the runtime patch we pushed to staging and agree next steps for canary.
[00:10] Dr. Anika Rao: thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround. our SLA for the clinical scoring is 150ms p95, we saw spikes to 800ms for a subset of requests for about three hours friday. that knocked a few pipelines.
[00:28] Marco Diaz: yeah the spike aligns with our batch re-ingest window, we were running large batches and noticed concurrent KV eviction events. logs show a higher-than-normal rekick.
[00:45] Jordan Li: so preliminary from our side, we saw two things: the runtime kernel selector occasionally picked a generic matmul path when sequence lengths were smaller which regressed perf, and also the K-V cash (transcription: kv cache) had a churn pattern that caused more cache misses under certain prefix distributions.
[01:05] Sana Patel: sorry can you explain the kernel selector bit again? is that about model config?
[01:12] Jordan Li: yeah it's at the runtime level. the heuristics that pick optimized kernels consider sequence length histograms, but if the histogram is noisy during heavy load it can mis-route to a slower path. we have a patch that forces the stable kernel for affected model family and adds a small hysteresis to the selector.
[01:32] Maya Chen: important to note the patch is conservative — it opts for the faster stable kernel but may increase slight memory usage in worst-case. we measured a 2-3% memory uptick on our staging nodes.
[01:46] Terry Ng: from security side, any changes that affect cryptographic key handling or network exposure? we need to sign off for private deploys.
[01:54] Jordan Li: no KMS changes; patch is purely inside the inference path. no new listeners. we'll provide a diff and a short security addendum.
[02:05] Marco Diaz: the other angle is background compaction on the host. during the window we had increased IO which, combined with kernel shift, may have amplified tail. can we reproduce with compaction simulated?
[02:20] Jordan Li: yes we can simulate compaction and replay the exact request traces. we've requested sanitized logs.
[02:27] Maya Chen: action: Jordan will run a KV prefix cache replay on a staging cluster with compaction toggled, and capture latency histograms and flame graphs.
[02:40] Dr. Anika Rao: timeline — we need this validated and on canary by next week to avoid any production regression during our Q4 reports.
[02:48] Felix Moreno: understood. Our proposal: run validation now, then a constrained canary to 5% of traffic with traffic shaping and fast rollback hooks; if stable, widen over 48 hours.
[03:04] Sana Patel: how do you define the canary window and rollback condition? we want concrete SLO gates.
[03:11] Maya Chen: recommended gates: p95 tail below 200ms and error rate no more than 0.05% above baseline for the canary window. rollback if any sustained 2x increase in p95 over 30m.
[03:26] Marco Diaz: sounds reasonable. we also need tracer IDs passed back — our ops need the exact spans to correlate traces.
[03:33] Jordan Li: will include tracing hooks, we'll also add extra logs for the prefix eviction counters.
[03:39] Terry Ng: and audit logs retention? we need proof of request lineage for compliance, 12 month retention.
[03:45] Felix Moreno: Redwood Console already supports long-term retention as an add-on; we'll outline options and costs in the follow-up.
[03:55] Dr. Anika Rao: one question — any risk the patch could affect model quality or tokenization? we've seen subtle shifts before when quant profiles change.
[04:03] Jordan Li: patch doesn't touch quant paths or tokenizer. it's orthogonal. but we'll run a small prompt suite to assert parity on outputs and token-level timing.
[04:16] Sana Patel: can we see an example runbook for canary and rollback?
[04:20] Maya Chen: yes we'll share a runbook template and add Arborium-specific steps (who presses rollback, who validates logs, slack/webhook channels).
[04:28] Marco Diaz: operationally, we want a hard rollback point within 10 minutes. is that achievable?
[04:33] Jordan Li: yes, the runtime supports immediate rollback to previous kernel config and we keep the previous model artifact pinned. it is a config flip, so low-latency rollback.
[04:44] Dr. Anika Rao: ok good. one more: procurement asked about third-party vendors; we need to know if any external libs are updated with the patch.
[04:53] Maya Chen: patch touches internal runtime heuristics and one vendor BLAS patch; we'll enumerate CVEs and vendor versions in the addendum.
[05:02] Felix Moreno: I'll take point on the postmortem doc and coordinate with your ops to finalize mitigations list and timeline.
[05:10] Sana Patel: please include any temporary mitigations we can apply if we see recurrence, e.g., stricter routing to dedicated pool for clinical workloads.
[05:18] Jordan Li: we can add an override route to pin clinical traffic to dedicated pool — that'll increase cost but gives isolation. we'll include cost delta estimates.
[05:29] Dr. Anika Rao: perfect. action items?
[05:33] Maya Chen: recap of owners: Jordan to run replay + flame graphs (due Nov 6); Marco to send tracer IDs and exact timestamps (due Nov 5); Maya to send postmortem template and security addendum (due Nov 5); Felix to coordinate internal triage and mitigation road map (due Nov 10).
[05:55] Terry Ng: thanks all, we'll review the security addendum and circle back.
[06:00] Maya Chen: that's it from us, thanks for the time. we'll share artifacts in the RFC folder (link shared in calendar).

Notes: transcript contains a few ASR errors ("K-V cash" for KV cache, "rekick" ambiguous). There was brief crosstalk around 03:30.

End of transcript.
